Drafts: a Philly wholesale pick-ONE fork, a 'tenants, termites, toilets' honest-landlord question, and a 'what if it takes 13 years?' patience question.

drafts.draft_en:
You're 28 with $40k saved and you live in Philly. Pick ONE:

• Wholesale houses and stack assignment fees
• Put it down on a duplex and live in one side
• Put it in an index fund and don't touch it

No "split it." Be brutally honest. Why that one?

Not advice. I want to see how you think.
drafts.pattern: Pick-ONE fork, same shape as the 372.0k original and its 56.5k copy (age + cash + three concrete options + 'be brutally honest'), localized to Philly and wholesaling. Asks for opinions, promises no returns.
drafts.video_tip: Talking head, 10s. Hold up three fingers, one per option, with each option on screen exactly as written. Caption every spoken word. End on 'Be brutally honest' and point at the camera.

drafts.draft_en:
Every landlord meets the 3 T's eventually: tenants, termites, toilets.

Which one cost you the most?

Wrong answers only, unless it's a real story. Then I want the real story.
drafts.pattern: Borrows the 'tenants, termites, toilets' contrast from Cardone's 42.9k RE vs BTC post, but turns it into an honest landlord question for replies. No BTC claim, no return claim.
drafts.video_tip: Fast cuts, 9s, at a Philly rowhome. Beat 1: knock on a door (tenants). Beat 2: tap a wood beam (termites). Beat 3: point at a toilet (toilets). End on the question on screen, captioned.

drafts.draft_en:
Everyone says "just buy and hold."

Okay. What if the thing you bought takes 13 years to get back to where you bought it?

Stocks have done it. Real estate has done it.

What keeps you holding when it's flat for a decade?
drafts.pattern: Rides HughInvests' 72.2k 'S&P 500 once took nearly 13 years to reach a new high' pushback. Asks about patience and holding through a flat stretch; makes no forecast or return promise.
drafts.video_tip: Screen record, 12s. Draw a flat line across your notes app, label it '13 years', then type 'What keeps you holding?' under it. Caption the voiceover.
